did: GATE-SWEEP in the Nov 11 coordinator run, on server #772 (priority: high). The issue said PR gate's 15-minute sweep never fired, but it did fire, just rarely: 3 runs in 13 hours. The real hole was the image bot's pull requests. GitHub creates their runs approval-required, keeps github-actions[bot] as their actor after approval, and fires no workflow_run when they finish, because GITHUB_TOKEN events start no workflow apart from workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch. So only that throttled schedule could ever decide their gate (#781). PR #783 gave every pull-request workflow a last job, Tell PR gate. It needs every other job, runs only for the bot on this repository's own heads, and workflow_dispatches the verdict. A dispatched verdict waits at most 3 minutes for runs whose only unfinished job is that one, then judges as before. pr_gate.py fails a workflow without the job, and its self-test holds this and the wait. Codex found two edge cases: fork heads have a read-only token, and a run's status can lag its jobs. Both were fixed, and the coordinator merged #783 as 4333e2b. Proven on bot PR #785: 6 Tell PR gate jobs, then a dispatched verdict wrote PR gate success 12 s after the last check, with no sweep involved. #772 is closed.

calls.title: How bot PRs' finishes reach PR gate
options: Each pull-request workflow ends with Tell PR gate, which workflow_dispatches the verdict
A GitHub App token for the bot's push, so its runs are ordinary
PR gate (open) waits in the job for bot heads, as the C69 fallback does
calls.why: It needs no new credential and holds no runner on checks that are still working, which is #762's point. The App token is a new credential and so the owner's call. Waiting in the job brings back #762's hold.
calls.undo: Remove the tell_gate jobs, the settle wait and the untold check from scripts/pr_gate.py. If an App token is adopted, these become unneeded.

calls.title: Fork heads
options: Skip Tell PR gate when the head is a fork's, and leave those to the sweep
calls.why: A fork's pull_request token is read-only, so the dispatch would fail and turn an otherwise green run red. Codex found this on #783.
calls.undo: Drop the head.repo.full_name clause from TELL_IF and the 8 workflows.

left: On a bot head, CodeQL's dynamic run can't carry a Tell PR gate. If it finishes after every other check, only the sweep decides the gate, which stays pending until then. That is rare, because it starts at the push and the other runs wait for approval.
GitHub's scheduler still skips most sweep slots here. Nothing but the CodeQL case depends on it now.
Owner's call: a GitHub App token for detect.yml's push would remove both the approval step and the need for Tell PR gate.
A bot PR's runs still need approval. POST /actions/runs/{id}/approve works and needs no re-run.
The calls above aren't in some-ui's docs/calls.json. This run's IDs C85 to C88 were offered for them.
